Hearing Recap: “Building an AI-Ready America: Higher Education in the Age of AI”
WASHINGTON, D.C.,
June 3, 2026
Today, the Subcommittee on Higher Education and Workforce Development held a hearing to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) is impacting higher education. This was the “AI can personalize instruction in ways that a single instructor teaching many students simply cannot do. It can identify students who are struggling before they fall behind. It can reduce the administrative burdens that consume faculty and staff time, freeing them to focus on students. AI can also help better align academic programs with the knowledge and skills employers need,” he said.
“When [AI is used] to support the kind of personalization we’ve discussed earlier, great! When it’s to do the cognitive automation where you’re not doing the work, that’s a huge problem,” said Innovation must be paired with responsibility. Clear policies and responsible implementation can help ensure AI strengthens, rather than undermines, educational outcomes. Rep. Randy Fine (R-FL) summarized the issue at hand perfectly. “We should welcome this inevitable reality—technology has changed how the world works since the horse and buggy. We didn’t look back, we looked forward and that’s what we need to do here as well. Our education system has a challenge—to prepare [our students] for the reality, not train them for the jobs that will no longer exist,” he said. |
